findings.title: Hung flusher process is never killed because the isinstance check is always False
findings.body: The new code guards the kill with `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Processes come from `mp_context.Process`, which is `SpawnProcess`. That class derives from `BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.context.Process`, so the check is always False. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally, so this is a regression. When a flusher is detected as hung (`cause == "hang"`), it stays alive and a replacement is started for the same shards. Two flushers then run on the same shards, which can produce duplicate segments and leak processes. The same wrong check in `join()` means `terminate()` is also never called. Use `hasattr(process, 'kill')`, check `isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` and invert it, or check `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`.

findings.title: join() skips terminating remaining processes when the deadline passes
findings.body: In the `join()` loop, `break` fires when the deadline has passed. This skips the `terminate()` call for every process not yet visited. With several flusher processes, one slow process can use up the whole timeout, and the others are left running until the interpreter exits. The loop should terminate all processes regardless of the deadline, or the deadline check should only skip the waiting.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: The test sets `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top. The added `time.sleep(0.1)`, commented as giving flusher threads time to process, therefore does nothing. `step.join()` then races against the flusher thread picking up the new drift. The `(msg,) = messages` assertion can be flaky. Use the real sleep, for example by saving a reference before patching, or poll until `messages` is non-empty with a timeout.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name: "shards" vs "shard"
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use the tag `shard`. `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `shards`. The value is a comma-joined list in all three. Dashboards that group by tag will not line up. In `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` the `shard` tag is a single int, which is a third meaning for the same tag name.

findings.title: Unused dead method _create_process_for_shard
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is never called. `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards` directly. Remove it.
